title: Help me not miss giving patients their meds on time
description: I keep getting pulled away to help with emergencies before I can give medications. Patients end up getting their meds late and I worry about their safety.
problemStatement: Medication administration delays are common on busy units. Nurses retrieve medications from Pyxis but often get pulled away for urgent patient needs before administering. Current Epic MAR does not alert in real-time, leading to delayed doses that impact patient outcomes. We see 15-20% of scheduled medications administered over 1 hour late on average.
proposedSolution: Enhance Epic Rover mobile carts with integrated Pyxis dispensing data. When nurse scans medication at Pyxis, system tracks it. If not scanned at bedside within 30 minutes, automated alert goes to charge nurse dashboard. Barcode verification at bedside confirms right patient, right med, right time - all documented automatically in Epic MAR.
expectedBenefit: Reduce late medication administration by 80%. Improve patient safety scores. Reduce nurse documentation time by 5 minutes per med pass. Decrease medication errors related to wrong patient/wrong med. Better compliance with Joint Commission standards.

title: Faster way to find wheelchairs
description: We waste so much time looking for wheelchairs. Can we put trackers on them?

title: Patient discharge takes forever
description: Families wait hours for discharge paperwork. There has to be a better way.
problemStatement: Average discharge time is 3-4 hours from when doctor writes order. Families get frustrated waiting. We need to turn beds faster.
proposedSolution: Maybe we could start the paperwork earlier? Or have a dedicated discharge nurse?
expectedBenefit: Faster discharges, happier patients, more available beds

title: Better way to track patient belongings
description: Patients lose their glasses, dentures, hearing aids all the time. We need a system.
problemStatement: Patient belongings get lost during transfers between units or to procedures. Family members complain. We have no good tracking system. Items are expensive to replace and important for patient dignity and function.
proposedSolution: Create a simple bag system with barcode labels. Scan items in when patient arrives, scan out when they leave. Track location in Epic. Take photos of items with patient's tablet. Alert if patient is being transferred and belongings haven't been scanned.
expectedBenefit: Reduce lost items by 90%. Improve patient satisfaction scores. Reduce complaints. Maintain patient dignity. Save families money on replacements.

title: IV pumps always alarming
description: The alarms drive everyone crazy and we miss real problems

title: Cafeteria food options for night shift
description: Nothing is open after 8pm. Night shift workers need healthy food options too.
problemStatement: Night shift staff (11pm-7am) have no access to hot meals or healthy food. Vending machines only have junk food. Staff bring food from home but no way to heat it up on some units. Affects morale and health.
proposedSolution: Keep cafeteria open 24/7 with limited menu, or at least have grab-and-go healthy options in refrigerated vending machines. Add more microwaves on units. Partner with local restaurants for late-night delivery.
expectedBenefit: Improve night shift satisfaction and retention. Better nutrition for staff. Show we care about all shifts equally.

title: Can't find interpreters when we need them
description: Language line takes forever and video interpreters are always busy
problemStatement: We serve diverse community with 40+ languages. Phone interpretation has poor audio quality. Video interpreters often have 15-20 minute wait times. Delays care and frustrates patients. Some staff use family members which is not appropriate for medical decisions.
proposedSolution: Invest in more video interpretation devices. Create on-call pool of in-person interpreters for common languages (Spanish, Creole, Portuguese). Use AI translation for simple phrases and written materials. Train more bilingual staff and pay differential.
expectedBenefit: Reduce interpretation wait times to under 5 minutes. Improve patient understanding and satisfaction. Better informed consent. Reduce medical errors from miscommunication. Meet Joint Commission requirements.

title: Parking is terrible
description: Staff park so far away. Patients can't find spots. Expensive too.

title: Wound care photos are inconsistent
description: Every nurse takes pictures differently. Hard to track healing progress.
problemStatement: Wound documentation varies widely between nurses. Some use phones, some use hospital cameras, some don't take photos at all. No standard for lighting, angle, or ruler placement. Makes it hard for wound care team to assess healing. Photos stored in different places - some in Epic, some on shared drive, some lost.
proposedSolution: Standardized wound photography protocol with AI assistance. App on hospital tablets that guides nurse through proper photo technique - ensures ruler is visible, lighting is consistent, multiple angles captured. AI automatically measures wound dimensions. Photos upload directly to Epic with date/time stamp. AI can track healing progress over time and alert if wound is getting worse.
expectedBenefit: Consistent wound documentation. Better tracking of healing. Earlier identification of problems. Reduce hospital-acquired pressure injuries. Better communication with wound care specialists. Legal protection with proper documentation.

title: New nurses need better orientation
description: They seem lost for months. We need a buddy system or something.
problemStatement: New graduate nurses take 6-9 months to feel confident. Current orientation is 6 weeks but not enough. Preceptors are burned out. High turnover in first year - we lose 30% of new grads. Expensive to recruit and train.
proposedSolution: Extended orientation program - 12 weeks instead of 6. Assign permanent mentor for first year. Create simulation scenarios for common emergencies. Monthly check-ins with nurse manager. Peer support groups. Reduce patient load for first 3 months.
expectedBenefit: Reduce new grad turnover from 30% to under 15%. Improve confidence and competence. Better patient safety. Reduce preceptor burnout. Save money on recruitment.

title: Supply room is always messy
description: Can't find what I need. Things are expired. No organization.

title: Patient education materials are outdated
description: We hand out photocopied papers from 10 years ago. Patients want videos and apps.
problemStatement: Current patient education is all paper handouts. Reading level too high for many patients. Not available in multiple languages. Patients lose the papers. No way to track if they actually read it. Younger patients want digital options.
proposedSolution: Create patient education app or portal. Short videos (2-3 min) explaining common conditions and procedures. Available in top 10 languages. Interactive quizzes to check understanding. Send to patient's phone or email. Track completion in Epic. Include medication instructions with pictures.
expectedBenefit: Improve patient understanding and compliance. Reduce readmissions from lack of understanding. Better patient satisfaction. Meet health literacy requirements. Reduce printing costs.

title: Lab results take too long in ED
description: Patients wait hours for basic labs. Can we speed this up?
problemStatement: Average lab turnaround time in ED is 90 minutes for basic metabolic panel. Patients wait in ED beds. Delays treatment decisions. ED gets backed up. Some patients leave without being seen.
proposedSolution: Point-of-care testing for basic labs in ED. Rapid COVID and flu tests already work well. Add basic metabolic panel, troponin, d-dimer. Results in 15 minutes. Still send confirmatory tests to main lab. Train ED nurses to run tests.
expectedBenefit: Reduce ED length of stay by 60 minutes. Faster treatment decisions. Reduce patients who leave without being seen. Improve patient satisfaction. Free up ED beds faster.

title: Computers are so slow
description: Epic takes forever to load. Freezes all the time. Wastes so much time.

title: Fall prevention program needs improvement
description: We still have too many patient falls. Current system isn't working.
problemStatement: Hospital-acquired falls are our #1 safety event. 5-8 falls per 1000 patient days. Current prevention is yellow socks and bed alarms. Alarms go off constantly so we ignore them. High-risk patients identified but interventions are inconsistent. Falls lead to injuries, longer stays, lawsuits.
proposedSolution: AI-powered fall risk assessment that updates in real-time based on medications, vitals, mental status. Smart bed sensors that detect when patient is trying to get up - alert goes to nurse's phone with patient name and room. Video monitoring for high-risk patients. Hourly rounding with documentation. Physical therapy consult for all high-risk patients within 24 hours.
expectedBenefit: Reduce falls by 50%. Reduce fall-related injuries by 70%. Improve patient safety scores. Reduce liability. Better staff response time. Less alarm fatigue.

title: Break rooms are depressing
description: We need better spaces to decompress. Maybe some plants and comfortable chairs?

title: Sepsis alerts are too sensitive
description: We get 50 alerts per day and most aren't real sepsis. Boy who cried wolf.
problemStatement: Epic sepsis screening tool flags 40-60 patients per day. Only 5-10% actually have sepsis. Nurses and doctors ignore alerts. Real sepsis cases get missed. Alert fatigue is real problem. Current criteria too broad.
proposedSolution: Use AI/machine learning to improve sepsis prediction. Look at trends over time, not just single values. Consider patient's baseline. Prioritize alerts - red for high probability, yellow for watch. Reduce false positives by 80%. Include clinical context like recent surgery or chronic conditions.
expectedBenefit: Reduce alert volume by 80%. Improve sepsis detection accuracy. Faster treatment for real sepsis. Reduce mortality. Less alert fatigue. Better antibiotic stewardship.

title: Scheduling system is confusing
description: Can never get my time off approved. System crashes. Can't swap shifts easily.
problemStatement: Current scheduling system (Kronos) is not user-friendly. Takes 10 clicks to request time off. Can't see who's working same shift. Shift swaps require manager approval even when coverage is fine. System doesn't account for skills or certifications. Leads to unsafe staffing.
proposedSolution: Modern scheduling app on phones. One-click time off requests. See full unit schedule. Direct shift swaps with coworkers (manager notified but auto-approved if coverage met). AI suggests optimal schedule based on skills, preferences, and patient acuity. Self-scheduling within guidelines.
expectedBenefit: Improve staff satisfaction. Reduce scheduling errors. Better work-life balance. Reduce manager time on scheduling by 50%. Ensure safe staffing levels. Reduce overtime costs.

title: Patients can't reach call button
description: Call lights fall on floor. Patients can't reach them. Safety issue.

title: Medication reconciliation takes forever
description: Patients don't know their meds. We call pharmacies. Takes 30-45 minutes per patient.
problemStatement: Medication reconciliation at admission is time-consuming and error-prone. Patients don't remember medication names or doses. Multiple pharmacies. Some meds are OTC or supplements. We call pharmacies but they're often closed or don't answer. Errors in med rec lead to adverse events.
proposedSolution: Connect to state prescription monitoring database. Pull patient's medication history automatically. Use AI to identify discrepancies. Show patient pictures of pills to confirm. Connect to major pharmacy chains' systems. Voice-to-text for patient to describe meds. Flag high-risk medications.
expectedBenefit: Reduce med rec time from 30 min to 5 min. Improve accuracy. Reduce medication errors at transitions of care. Better patient safety. Nurse time savings. Meet Joint Commission requirements.

title: Hand hygiene compliance is low
description: We all know we should wash hands more but we forget when we're busy
problemStatement: Hand hygiene compliance is 65% but should be 95%+. Leads to hospital-acquired infections. Current monitoring is manual observation which is biased. Alcohol foam dispensers don't track usage. Staff forget when rushing between patients.
proposedSolution: Electronic hand hygiene monitoring system. Badge sensors track when staff enter/exit rooms and if they used sanitizer. Real-time feedback on badge - vibrates if you forget. Dashboard shows compliance by unit and individual. Gamification - rewards for high compliance. No punitive measures, just positive reinforcement.
expectedBenefit: Increase hand hygiene compliance to 95%. Reduce hospital-acquired infections by 30%. Improve patient safety. Meet regulatory requirements. Reduce C.diff and MRSA rates. Save lives.

title: Need better mental health support for staff
description: We see traumatic things every day. Need counseling and support groups.

title: Bedside shift report is awkward
description: Patients and families hear everything. Need privacy for sensitive info.
problemStatement: Bedside shift report improves patient safety but creates privacy issues. Can't discuss mental health, substance abuse, domestic violence, HIV status at bedside. Families interrupt with questions. Takes longer than report room. Some patients are sleeping and we wake them up.
proposedSolution: Hybrid approach - do bedside introduction and safety check (IV sites, fall risk, pain level) then step out for sensitive information. Use Epic handoff tool on tablets. Record key points so oncoming nurse can review. Allow patient to opt out of bedside report if they prefer.
expectedBenefit: Maintain patient safety benefits of bedside report while protecting privacy. Reduce HIPAA violations. Improve nurse satisfaction. More efficient handoffs. Better patient sleep.

title: Visitors don't follow rules
description: Too many visitors. They're loud. Don't wash hands. Bring in outside food.

title: Radiology transport delays are constant
description: Patients wait hours for CT scans. Transport is always backed up. Delays diagnosis.
problemStatement: Average wait time for stat CT in ED is 2-3 hours. Transport team is understaffed. Patients wait in ED or on floors. Delays diagnosis and treatment. Some patients deteriorate while waiting. Radiology has open slots but can't get patients there.
proposedSolution: Uber-style transport system. All transport requests go into queue with priority levels. Real-time tracking of transport staff locations. AI optimizes routes and assignments. Patients and nurses can see estimated wait time. Add more transport staff during peak hours (10am-4pm). Cross-train other staff to help with transport.
expectedBenefit: Reduce transport wait times by 60%. Faster diagnosis and treatment. Improve ED throughput. Better patient outcomes. Reduce staff frustration. More efficient use of radiology capacity.

title: Glucose meters are unreliable
description: Get different readings from different meters. Patients don't trust them.

title: Discharge prescriptions get lost
description: We send prescriptions to pharmacy but patients say they never got them. Communication breakdown.
problemStatement: 30% of discharge prescriptions have issues - sent to wrong pharmacy, insurance doesn't cover, patient can't afford, pharmacy is closed. Patients leave hospital without medications. Leads to readmissions. No good tracking system. Patients don't know prescriptions were sent.
proposedSolution: Integrated discharge prescription system. Check insurance formulary before prescribing. Show patient out-of-pocket cost. Let patient choose pharmacy. Send text when prescription is ready. Pharmacist reviews before patient leaves hospital. For high-risk meds, give first dose before discharge. Follow-up call next day to confirm patient picked up meds.
expectedBenefit: Reduce prescription-related readmissions by 40%. Improve medication adherence. Better patient satisfaction. Reduce ED visits for medication issues. Save patients money. Meet CMS requirements.

title: Need better way to communicate with deaf patients
description: Video interpreters are hard to use. Patients get frustrated. We need something better.
problemStatement: Deaf and hard-of-hearing patients face communication barriers. Video interpreters have technical issues. Not all staff know how to use them. Some patients prefer written communication. Delays care and creates safety risks. Patients feel isolated and frustrated.
proposedSolution: Multiple communication options - improve video interpreter technology, provide tablets with typing interface, use AI for real-time captioning, train more staff in basic sign language, hire deaf patient navigators, use visual aids and pictures for common needs.
expectedBenefit: Improve communication with deaf patients. Better patient safety. Reduce medical errors. Improve patient satisfaction. Meet ADA requirements. More inclusive care environment.

title: OR turnover time is too long
description: Between cases we waste 45 minutes. Could do more surgeries if we were faster.
problemStatement: Average OR turnover time is 45 minutes. Should be 20-25 minutes. Delays surgery schedule. Patients wait longer. Surgeons get frustrated. Lost revenue from fewer cases per day. Cleaning is thorough but inefficient. Equipment not ready. Communication gaps between teams.
proposedSolution: Standardize turnover process with checklist. Parallel processing - start cleaning while documenting previous case. Pre-position equipment for next case. Dedicated turnover team. Real-time dashboard showing turnover status. Incentivize fast turnovers. Identify bottlenecks with time-motion study.
expectedBenefit: Reduce turnover time to 25 minutes. Add 2-3 more cases per OR per day. Increase revenue by $2-3M annually. Reduce patient wait times. Improve surgeon satisfaction. Better OR utilization.

title: Nurses station is too far from patient rooms
description: We walk miles every shift. Wear out our feet and knees. Takes time away from patients.

title: Patient portal is confusing
description: Patients can't figure out how to use it. Too many clicks. Need simpler design.
problemStatement: Only 40% of patients use patient portal. Older patients especially struggle. Too many features buried in menus. Can't find test results or appointment info. Password reset is complicated. Mobile app is clunky. Patients call instead of using portal.
proposedSolution: Redesign portal with user-friendly interface. Put most common tasks on home screen - view test results, message doctor, schedule appointment, request prescription refills. Simplify navigation. Better mobile app. Video tutorials. In-person training at clinics. Biometric login option.
expectedBenefit: Increase portal usage to 75%. Reduce phone calls to clinics by 30%. Improve patient engagement. Better access to health information. Reduce staff workload. Improve patient satisfaction scores.

title: Blood sugar checks hurt patients
description: Finger sticks 4 times a day. Patients hate it. Their fingers get sore. Maybe continuous monitors?
problemStatement: Diabetic patients get finger stick blood sugar checks 4-6 times per day. Painful and inconvenient. Fingers get calloused and sore. Some patients refuse checks. Nurses spend 5 minutes per check. Continuous glucose monitors (CGMs) exist but not used in hospital.
proposedSolution: Pilot program using CGMs for hospitalized diabetics. Apply sensor on admission, wear for entire stay. Real-time glucose data in Epic. Alerts for high/low values. Still do finger sticks for confirmation of critical values. Train nurses on CGM technology. Work with insurance for coverage.
expectedBenefit: Reduce patient discomfort and improve satisfaction. Better glucose control with real-time data. Reduce hypoglycemic events. Save nurse time - 20 minutes per patient per day. Earlier detection of glucose trends. Better diabetes management.

title: Staff don't know about new policies
description: Things change all the time. We get emails but who reads them all? Need better communication.

title: Patients don't understand their bills
description: They get huge bills and don't know what they're paying for. Leads to complaints and non-payment.
problemStatement: Hospital bills are confusing and overwhelming. Patients don't understand charges. Multiple bills from different providers. Insurance explanation of benefits is unclear. Patients shocked by out-of-pocket costs. Leads to bad debt and patient dissatisfaction. Financial counseling is limited.
proposedSolution: Transparent pricing tool - show estimated costs before procedures. Plain-language bills with explanations. Consolidate bills when possible. Financial counselors meet with patients before discharge. Payment plans with no interest. Charity care screening for eligible patients. Text/email reminders about bills.
expectedBenefit: Improve patient understanding of costs. Reduce billing complaints by 50%. Increase collections rate. Better patient satisfaction. Reduce bad debt. Meet price transparency requirements. Improve financial counseling access.

title: Ventilator weaning takes too long
description: Patients stay on vents longer than needed. Need better protocols and monitoring.
problemStatement: Average ventilator days in ICU is 5.2, should be closer to 3.5. Prolonged ventilation increases pneumonia risk, delirium, and costs. Current weaning protocols are not consistently followed. Respiratory therapists are busy. Daily spontaneous breathing trials often missed.
proposedSolution: AI-assisted ventilator weaning. System analyzes patient data (vitals, labs, sedation level) and recommends when to start weaning. Automated reminders for spontaneous breathing trials. Real-time monitoring of weaning progress. Alert if patient not progressing as expected. Standardized protocol with built-in decision support.
expectedBenefit: Reduce average ventilator days by 30%. Reduce ventilator-associated pneumonia. Reduce ICU length of stay. Lower costs. Improve patient outcomes. Free up ICU beds. Reduce delirium and long-term complications.

title: Pharmacy is always out of common meds
description: We order meds and they're on backorder. Have to use alternatives. Confusing for patients.

title: Telemetry monitoring is overwhelming
description: One tech watches 48 patients. Alarms constantly. Can't keep up. Miss important rhythms.
problemStatement: Telemetry techs monitor 40-48 patients each. Alarm fatigue is severe - 90% of alarms are false. Important arrhythmias can be missed. Techs are burned out. Current system flags every artifact and lead issue. Delays in notifying nurses about critical rhythms.
proposedSolution: AI-powered telemetry monitoring. Machine learning filters out false alarms and artifacts. Prioritizes critical rhythms (V-tach, V-fib, asystole). Sends alerts directly to nurse's phone with ECG strip. Reduces tech workload. Predictive analytics for patients at risk of arrhythmias. Better alarm management.
expectedBenefit: Reduce false alarms by 80%. Faster response to critical rhythms. Reduce tech burnout. Improve patient safety. Earlier detection of deterioration. Better nurse workflow. Reduce cardiac arrests.

title: Need better lactation support
description: New moms struggle with breastfeeding. Not enough lactation consultants. They wait days for help.
problemStatement: Only 2 lactation consultants for entire hospital. New mothers wait 24-48 hours for help. Many give up on breastfeeding. Affects baby bonding and nutrition. Nurses try to help but don't have specialized training. Leads to early formula supplementation and lower breastfeeding rates.
proposedSolution: Hire more lactation consultants - goal of seeing every new mom within 4 hours of delivery. Train postpartum nurses in basic lactation support. Virtual lactation visits via video for night shift. Peer support groups. Lactation clinic for outpatient follow-up. Provide breast pumps and supplies.
expectedBenefit: Increase exclusive breastfeeding rate from 60% to 80%. Improve mother satisfaction. Better baby health outcomes. Meet Baby-Friendly Hospital designation. Reduce formula costs. Support for working mothers.

title: Elevators are always broken
description: We wait forever for elevators. Patients on stretchers can't fit. Delays everything.

title: Pressure injury prevention needs work
description: We still get too many stage 3 and 4 pressure injuries. Current prevention isn't enough.
problemStatement: Hospital-acquired pressure injuries (HAPIs) occur in 3-5% of patients. Stage 3 and 4 injuries are never events. Current prevention is turning patients every 2 hours and special mattresses. Compliance with turning is inconsistent. High-risk patients not always identified. Leads to patient suffering, longer stays, and liability.
proposedSolution: Smart bed technology that monitors patient position and automatically alerts when turning is due. AI risk assessment that updates based on patient condition. Pressure-mapping technology shows high-risk areas. Dedicated skin care team for high-risk patients. Better documentation of prevention measures. Incontinence management program.
expectedBenefit: Reduce HAPIs by 60%. Eliminate stage 3 and 4 injuries. Improve patient outcomes. Reduce costs from extended stays. Reduce liability. Better regulatory compliance. Improve nurse accountability.

title: Staff badges don't work half the time
description: Can't get into locked units. Have to wait for someone to let me in. Security issue.

title: Antibiotic stewardship is inconsistent
description: Docs prescribe broad-spectrum antibiotics for everything. Need better guidelines and oversight.
problemStatement: Antibiotic overuse leads to resistance. C.diff rates are high. Broad-spectrum antibiotics used when narrow-spectrum would work. Antibiotics continued longer than needed. Stewardship team is small and can't review all cases. Need better decision support and education.
proposedSolution: AI-powered antibiotic stewardship. System analyzes patient data and suggests appropriate antibiotic based on likely organism, local resistance patterns, and patient factors. Alerts when antibiotics should be de-escalated or stopped. Automatic stop dates. Pharmacist review of all broad-spectrum antibiotics. Education for prescribers.
expectedBenefit: Reduce inappropriate antibiotic use by 40%. Reduce C.diff infections by 30%. Reduce antibiotic resistance. Lower pharmacy costs. Improve patient outcomes. Meet Joint Commission requirements. Better antimicrobial stewardship metrics.

title: Patients don't get enough sleep
description: We wake them up all night for vitals and meds. They're exhausted. Need to cluster care better.
problemStatement: Hospitalized patients average only 4-5 hours of sleep per night. Interrupted by vital signs, medications, lab draws, alarms, noise. Sleep deprivation delays healing, increases delirium, and lowers satisfaction. Current practice is vitals every 4 hours around the clock for all patients.
proposedSolution: Risk-stratify patients - stable patients get vitals every 6-8 hours at night. Cluster care - do vitals, meds, and assessments together. Quiet hours 10pm-6am with reduced noise and lights. Wireless monitoring for high-risk patients. Reschedule non-urgent meds to daytime. Sound-absorbing materials in hallways.
expectedBenefit: Increase patient sleep to 6-7 hours per night. Reduce delirium by 30%. Improve patient satisfaction scores. Faster recovery. Reduce length of stay. Better patient experience. Reduce nurse interruptions at night.

title: Medical records are incomplete
description: Outside records don't transfer. We don't know patient's history. Have to repeat tests.

title: Pediatric pain assessment is challenging
description: Young kids can't tell us their pain level. Need better tools for non-verbal patients.
problemStatement: Current pain scales don't work well for children under 5, non-verbal patients, or patients with cognitive impairment. We rely on behavioral cues but these are subjective. Under-treatment of pain is common. Parents are frustrated. Affects patient comfort and healing.
proposedSolution: Implement validated pediatric pain scales (FLACC for infants, Wong-Baker faces for kids). Train all staff on pain assessment. Use AI to analyze facial expressions and body language. Parent input on pain assessment. Regular pain reassessment. Non-pharmacologic pain management options (distraction, comfort positioning, cold/heat).
expectedBenefit: Improve pain management for vulnerable populations. Better patient comfort. Reduce parent anxiety. Improve satisfaction scores. Better pain documentation. Appropriate pain medication use. Improved healing.

title: Rapid response team is too slow
description: When we call a rapid, it takes 10-15 minutes for team to arrive. Patients deteriorate fast.
problemStatement: Average rapid response team arrival time is 12 minutes. Should be under 5 minutes. Team members are scattered across hospital. Pagers don't always work. Delays in critical interventions. Some patients code before team arrives. Nurses feel unsupported.
proposedSolution: Dedicated rapid response team on each shift - not pulled for other duties. Team stays in central location. Phone app alerts all team members simultaneously with room number and patient info. Pre-positioned equipment carts on each floor. Predictive analytics to identify patients at risk before they deteriorate. Proactive rounding on high-risk patients.
expectedBenefit: Reduce response time to under 5 minutes. Reduce code blues by 40%. Improve patient outcomes. Reduce ICU transfers. Better nurse confidence. Earlier intervention for deteriorating patients. Reduce mortality.

title: Clinic wait times are ridiculous
description: Patients wait an hour past their appointment time. They get angry. We're always behind schedule.
problemStatement: Average clinic wait time is 45-60 minutes past scheduled appointment. Overbooking is common. Providers run behind. Patients are frustrated and leave bad reviews. Some patients leave without being seen. Affects patient satisfaction and clinic reputation.
proposedSolution: Better scheduling algorithms that account for visit complexity. Buffer time between appointments. Text patients when provider is running late. Offer virtual visits for simple issues. Reduce no-shows with reminder texts. Analyze schedule patterns to identify bottlenecks. Hire more medical assistants to improve rooming efficiency.
expectedBenefit: Reduce wait times to under 15 minutes. Improve patient satisfaction scores. Reduce no-shows. Better provider satisfaction. More efficient clinic operations. Increase patient volume. Better reviews and reputation.

title: Surgical site infections are too common
description: We need better pre-op protocols and post-op monitoring to prevent infections.
problemStatement: Surgical site infection (SSI) rate is 2.5%, should be under 1%. Leads to readmissions, reoperations, and patient suffering. Current prevention includes antibiotics and skin prep but not standardized. Post-discharge monitoring is limited. Some infections not caught until patient is very sick.
proposedSolution: Standardized pre-op protocol - chlorhexidine showers, nasal decolonization for high-risk patients, proper antibiotic timing. Intra-op bundle - maintain normothermia, glucose control, appropriate skin prep. Post-op surveillance - wound photos at discharge, text-based monitoring, early follow-up for high-risk patients. AI analysis of risk factors.
expectedBenefit: Reduce SSI rate to under 1%. Reduce readmissions by 30%. Improve patient outcomes. Lower costs from complications. Better surgical quality metrics. Meet CMS requirements. Reduce patient suffering and mortality.

title: Staff don't know how to use new equipment
description: We get new devices but no training. Figure it out as we go. Seems unsafe.

title: Readmission rates are too high
description: Patients come back within 30 days. We need better discharge planning and follow-up.
problemStatement: 30-day readmission rate is 18%, should be under 12%. Costs hospital millions in penalties. Common reasons - medication issues, lack of follow-up, worsening chronic conditions, inadequate patient education. Current discharge planning is rushed. No systematic follow-up after discharge.
proposedSolution: Comprehensive discharge program - pharmacist medication review, teach-back method for patient education, schedule follow-up appointment before discharge, post-discharge phone calls at 48 hours and 7 days, home health for high-risk patients, transition clinic for urgent issues, predictive analytics to identify high-risk patients.
expectedBenefit: Reduce readmissions to under 12%. Save $5-8M annually in penalties. Improve patient outcomes. Better care transitions. Reduce ED visits. Improve patient satisfaction. Meet CMS quality metrics. Better chronic disease management.
